title: Abandoned Cart and Win-Back Automation
summary: Recover abandoned carts and bring back lapsed customers with WhatsApp and email journeys built around cart contents and purchase cycles, measured against a holdout group.

seo.title: Abandoned Cart and Win-Back Automation | VipraTech
seo.description: WhatsApp and email journeys for D2C brands that recover abandoned carts and win back lapsed buyers, tailored by cart and purchase cycle, with holdouts.

problem.intro: Most visitors who add to cart do not buy, and many first-time customers never order again. Brands respond with the same discount reminder for everyone, which costs margin, trains customers to wait for a coupon and fills WhatsApp with messages people block.

pain_points.title: Generic reminders
pain_points.detail: Every abandoner gets the same message and coupon, regardless of what they left, why, or whether they would have returned anyway.

pain_points.title: Discount dependence
pain_points.detail: Coupons in every reminder erode margin and teach customers to abandon on purpose.

pain_points.title: WhatsApp quality risk
pain_points.detail: High message volumes with low relevance lead to blocks and reports that hurt your sender quality rating.

pain_points.title: No proof of impact
pain_points.detail: Recovered orders are counted without a holdout, so nobody knows which would have happened without the message.

solution.overview: We build journeys that react to what each customer did. An abandoned cart triggers a WhatsApp or email reminder that shows the actual items, addresses common blockers such as size, delivery time to their pincode or COD availability, and answers replies conversationally, handing anything outside scope to support. Win-back journeys follow each customer's purchase cycle, so a replenishment reminder for a moisturiser arrives around when it is likely to run out. An LLM drafts message variants in your brand voice from approved building blocks, and incentives come only from approved coupon pools. Every journey keeps a holdout group, so impact is measured rather than assumed.
capabilities: Cart and browse abandonment triggers from Shopify, WooCommerce or your storefront
Messages that show the actual cart items, sizes in stock and delivery time to the customer's pincode
Conversational replies on WhatsApp for size, delivery and COD questions, with handover to support
Win-back timing based on each customer's purchase cycle and category
Message variants drafted in your brand voice from approved templates and claims
Built-in holdout groups, frequency caps and quiet hours

workflow.title: Capture events
workflow.detail: Cart, checkout, browse and order events stream from your storefront and OMS.

workflow.title: Select eligible customers
workflow.detail: Opt-in status, frequency caps, recent orders and holdout assignment decide who receives a message.

workflow.title: Compose the message
workflow.detail: The message is built from the cart or purchase history, approved templates and any approved incentive.

workflow.title: Send and converse
workflow.detail: WhatsApp or email goes out, and replies are answered within scope or handed to support.

workflow.title: Measure against holdout
workflow.detail: Orders from messaged customers are compared with the holdout group.

workflow.title: Marketing review
workflow.detail: Marketing reviews results, opt-outs and quality rating weekly and approves template or rule changes.

inputs: Cart, checkout, browse and order events
Order history by customer and category
Approved templates, claims and coupon pools
outputs: Abandoned cart and win-back messages tailored to each customer
Holdout comparison of conversion and revenue
Opt-out, block and quality rating reports
Message variant performance for marketing review
human_in_the_loop: Marketing approves templates, claims, incentive rules and journey changes before they go live, and reviews results weekly. Replies outside the agreed FAQ scope go to a support agent.
integrations: Email service or a marketing automation platform such as Klaviyo, MoEngage or CleverTap
guardrails: Messages only to opted-in customers, with frequency caps and quiet hours
Incentives only from approved coupon pools
No false urgency or fake scarcity in copy
Holdout group maintained for every journey
compliance_notes: Marketing messages rely on consent that customers can withdraw, as the DPDP Act 2023 requires.
Copy avoids false urgency and other practices listed in the CCPA dark-pattern guidelines.
SMS fallbacks use DLT-registered headers and templates under TRAI rules.

pilot.scope: The abandoned cart journey on WhatsApp for one storefront, with a randomly assigned holdout group, plus one win-back journey for a replenishment category.
deliverables: Journey designs and templates approved by marketing
Working triggers, decisioning and WhatsApp flows
Roll-out plan and messaging cost estimate

what_we_measure.how: Conversion of messaged customers compared with the holdout group.
Messaging and incentive cost divided by orders above the holdout baseline.
Opt-outs, blocks and quality rating changes per thousand messages sent.
A sample of conversational replies reviewed for correctness and handover decisions.

faqs.q: Why not just send a coupon to everyone who abandons?
faqs.a: Because many would have bought anyway, and blanket coupons teach customers to wait. The holdout shows how many orders the reminder actually adds, so incentives can be kept for segments where they make a difference.

faqs.q: Will this hurt our WhatsApp quality rating?
faqs.a: It is designed to protect it: messages go only to opted-in customers, relate to what they did, and are capped. We monitor blocks and the quality rating weekly during the pilot.

faqs.q: Can the assistant answer replies like 'is size M available?'
faqs.a: Yes, from live inventory and your FAQ content. Anything outside that scope, such as a complaint, goes to a support agent.
No. Storefront and OMS events are enough to start. If you already use a marketing automation platform, we connect to it rather than replace it.
